analysis:
Examined both added test files, their metadata and patches, and the cluster test excerpt plus its fixture-refactor patch. No concrete security regression is established by this test-only scope. ClusterServiceRestartingStopTests.swift:426–669 exercises command-lock serialization, stopped/handed-over claim checks, failed-stop restoration and retry throttling (A-018); its only mapped change replaces setup with startedLeaderService at head line 32, whose implementation is outside this batch.
LoopExitThinkingContinuationTests.swift:96–183 asserts reconstruction from the original prompt and generated tokens, remaining-budget accounting and answer caps. Lines 186–294 exercise cancellation before/during continuation, consumer departure, and aggregation of usage and failures. GenerationLoopExitThinkingServingTests.swift tests scheduler/bridge integration, reasoning separation, usage aggregation, row-release cleanup and delayed retirement under whole-Mac capacity pressure. Engines and prompts are synthetic; the new code does not itself expose production plaintext, credentials or privileged authority.
Integration must verify the actual LoopExitThinkingContinuation, scheduler and EngineV2Bridge changes: cancellation reaches the second row (T-010), capacity/KV reservations retire before resubmission (A-018), continuation retains coordinator-authored cacheSalt and model bindings (T-041), and aggregated terminal/usage events preserve coordinator billing semantics (A-009). Also confirm a continuation cannot outlive serving authorization/revocation (T-053) and stays within the encrypted response path (T-008). The tests establish intended behavior, not those production contracts; absent implementations are coverage limits, not findings.
